one_sentence_failure_summary: An external SSH daemon (OpenSSH 7.4) pre-bound to port 22 in the shared-network container prevents the agent from placing its own sshd on the required default port, and all workaround attempts (socat forwarding, iptables NAT redirection) are blocked by missing kernel capabilities, leaving SSH-over-port-22 permanently unsatisfied.
t_err_evidence: service ssh start ... Starting OpenBSD Secure Shell server sshd [ OK ] (committed to own sshd serving port 22 for git)
t_commit_evidence: At step 230, iptables-legacy returns 'getsockopt failed strangely: Operation not permitted', exhausting the last viable workaround class (NAT redirection). At this point socat binding to port 22 has already failed (step 200 onward) and NET_ADMIN capabilities are confirmed missing, locking in the failure: the agent cannot redirect port 22 traffic to its sshd on 2222 and cannot make any further progress toward the port-22 requirement.
t_surface_evidence: kex_exchange_identification: read: Connection reset by peer / Connection reset by ::1 port 22
trigger_explanation: The container runs with a shared network namespace exposing the host's OpenSSH 7.4 daemon on all interfaces at port 22. This is a real environment blocker (not an agent misconception). The agent correctly identifies the obstacle at step 165 but then handles it wrongly: it attempts socat port forwarding (step 200, fails because port 22 is already bound), iptables NAT rules (steps 215-230, fail because CAP_NET_ADMIN is absent), and repeated port toggling (steps 175-260), rather than finding any viable resolution. None of these workarounds succeed, and the outcome is failure on the SSH requirement.
forewarning_evidence: System has not been booted with systemd as init system (PID 1). Can't operate.
